name: Bakelite AD36 radio cabinet
summary: The Ekco AD36 domestic radio, on sale in Britain by 1935, was housed in a circular moulded Bakelite cabinet rather than a wooden case.
description: A circular molded phenol-formaldehyde cabinet used in Ekco’s AD36 domestic radio receiver.
tier_reason: A distinct materials application, regional technique or specialist branch.
why: Ekco was competing in the growing British home-radio market and carried forward the round moulded-Bakelite cabinet style it had already introduced on earlier sets.
